issues.title: Support a single message encrypted for multiple members
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body: As discussed at IETF 125, having a single TargetedMessage encrypted for multiple members at once, insures that if a single message is decrypted by multiple members, it had the same plaintext. This is a very desirable property. A client that does not want this property could sstill send distinct TargetedMessages with different plaintext to different members.

comments.author: raphaelrobert
comments.body:
Targeted Messages are meant as a building block to build exactly this kind of extended functionality. An application can just create on common ciphertext and use TMs to encrypt the corresponding key to several recipients.
Adding this functionality to the base construction would not make it more efficient due to how HPKE works.
In other words, I don't think we should include this because applications can already trivially do this.

comments.author: rohanmahy
comments.body:
> Targeted Messages are meant as a building block to build exactly this kind of extended functionality. An application can just create on common ciphertext and use TMs to encrypt the corresponding key to several recipients. Adding this functionality to the base construction would not make it more efficient due to how HPKE works. In other words, I don't think we should include this because applications can already trivially do this.

This is not trivial at all. The problem is sending a ciphertext that is verifiably common but does not leak the sender and recipient to other members of the group. Unless you have a signed wire format that binds this all together you are unlikely to get those properties.

Think about it this way: Given an honest DS, two members that receive a valid targeted message with the same sender, epoch, and generation are assured that they received the same plaintext.

comments.author: rohanmahy
comments.body: We can improve on the "honest DS" part as well with an AppAck-like mechanism or application-level mechanisms.

comments.author: raphaelrobert
comments.body:
I'm not sure I follow your thoughts, especially the part about the "honest DS". If a DS is honest, what exactly are you worried about?

First, a few clarifications on metadata:
 - TMs encrypt the sender inside `encrypted_sender_auth_data`, so that an adversary that's not a group member cannot tell who the sender is by just looking at the TM. This aligns with the base protocol, which in turn mirrors Signal's sealed-sender concept.
 - TMs *do not* encrypt the recipient, as the DS needs this information to forward the TM to the recipient. Without it, the DS would have to forward a TM to everyone in the group. Note that the recipient is represented only by the leaf index, which makes it somewhat pseudonymous, depending on the app's architecture.

I think it would help structure the discussion if you answered the following questions:
 - What exactly is your threat model? What capabilities does an attacker have?
 - What security guarantees would you like to achieve? In particular, how do they differ from what you already get today by sending 3 TMs with a wrapped key and one ciphertext?
 - TMs are based on HPKE, to stay aligned with the base protocol. HPKE is fundamentally a two-party protocol. What construction are you proposing instead?

issues.title: Consider including ContentType
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mahy-mls-new-content-types/ defines new `status` and `ephemeral` content types. It would be useful to be able to send such content types inside a TargetedMesage.

comments.author: raphaelrobert
comments.body:
The content of TMs is not structured on purpose so that it aligns with application messages and I think we should keep it that way.

I also think that TMs would be a terribly inefficient way to convey ephemeral messages.

issues.title: TargetedMessageTBS does not include application data
issues.author: istankovic
issues.body:
The first paragraph in "Signature Verification Before Processing" says:
```
The decryption flow necessarily produces plaintext before the signature can be
verified: the recipient first decrypts the sender authentication data
({{sender-data-encryption}}) to obtain the sender's leaf index, KEM output,
and signature, then decrypts the HPKE ciphertext to obtain the
`TargetedMessageContent`, and finally verifies the signature over the
`TargetedMessageTBS` structure.
```

From what I can tell, `TargetedMessageTBS` does not include application data, but the above paragraph implies that it does.
The way structures are defined, would it not be possible to first decrypt sender auth data, then verify the signature over `TargetedMessageTBS`, which includes `kem_output`, and then finally use `kem_output` to decrypt application data?

comments.author: raphaelrobert
comments.body: Good catch, the spec had not caught up with the code, and that part is now fixed in #7.

issues.title: Say how support for mls_targeted_message is signalled
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
The draft defines the `mls_targeted_message` wire format (L68) but not how a sender knows a recipient can process it. extensions-10 §5 provides `supported_wire_formats` and `required_wire_formats`, and its changelog says the old targeted_messages_capability is "now signaled using support_wire_formats and required_wire_formats", but this draft doesn't reference extensions-10.

Suggest a normative reference to draft-ietf-mls-extensions and a rule: a sender MUST NOT send a TargetedMessage to a member whose LeafNode doesn't list `mls_targeted_message` in `supported_wire_formats`, unless the GroupContext's `required_wire_formats` includes it.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-targeted-messages.md at ae3ab52.

issues.title: Forward Secrecy: leaf keys don't rotate per epoch
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
L450-456 says forward secrecy is "at epoch granularity", depends on "the recipient deleting the previous epoch's leaf private key", and that applications "SHOULD advance the epoch frequently". Under RFC 9420 a leaf's HPKE key changes only when that member updates its own leaf (Update, or a Commit whose path covers it); other members' Commits advance the epoch without touching it. So advancing the epoch doesn't rotate the recipient's key, and there's no per-epoch leaf key to delete.

Suggest saying decryption needs both the recipient's leaf private key and that epoch's exporter-derived PSK, that forward secrecy depends on deleting old epoch secrets and on the recipient updating its own leaf, and replacing "advance the epoch frequently" with a SHOULD that recipients update their leaf regularly.

Found reviewing -01 for mimid. Lines are draft-ietf-mls-targeted-messages.md at ae3ab52.

pulls.title: Editorial fixes from an implementation review
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Editorial fixes found reviewing -01. No wire format or requirement changes.

- Expand KEM, KDF and AEAD at first use (§4.2), and use the short forms later in §6.3.
- The `TargetedMessageContext` passed to SealPSK/OpenPSK is HPKE's `info` parameter (RFC 9180), so call it that; `hpke_context` → `hpke_info` in the prose and pseudocode. Same bytes.
- RFC 9420 §6.3.2's struct is `SenderData`, not `MLSSenderData` (two places).
- "OPTIONAL, accepting" comma splice → semicolon.
- Lowercase "forward secrecy" and "post-compromise security" in running text; section titles unchanged.
- Expand MTI in the test-vector section.

Left alone: the empty Acknowledgments section, which is yours to fill or drop.

Not built locally (no kramdown-rfc here).

pulls.title: Specify how mls_targeted_message support is signalled
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #11.

Adds a normative reference to draft-ietf-mls-extensions, says support is signalled with `supported_wire_formats` and `required_wire_formats`, and adds the rule: a sender MUST NOT send a TargetedMessage to a member whose LeafNode doesn't list `mls_targeted_message`, unless the GroupContext's `required_wire_formats` includes it.

pulls.title: Correct forward secrecy: leaf keys don't rotate per epoch
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Fixes #12.

The Forward Secrecy section now says decryption needs both the recipient's leaf private key and that epoch's exported secrets, that a leaf key changes only when its owner updates it, and replaces "SHOULD advance the epoch frequently" with a SHOULD that members update their own leaf regularly. The Authentication paragraph's line that the key schedule's FS/PCS guarantees "extend to targeted messages" may want softening to match; I left it out of scope.

pulls.title: Low-severity fixes from an implementation review
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Low-severity fixes from reviewing -01 for mimid; each is independent, so drop any you don't want.

- Authentication: the text said the key schedule's forward secrecy and post-compromise security "extend to targeted messages", but the exported secrets are valid for a whole epoch, so the sentence now says the guarantee holds only at epoch granularity and points to the Forward Secrecy section.
- Sender Identity Confidentiality: the section covered only the sender, so a new paragraph notes that `recipient_leaf_index` is sent in the clear and lets a Delivery Service that has the ratchet tree identify each message's recipient, and that padding hides only length, so hiding recipients needs measures such as cover traffic.

Not changed here: whether `TargetedMessage.authenticated_data` must be framed as SafeAAD when the group has `safe_aad` (extensions-10 §5 says AAD "always starts with" SafeAAD, which clashes with the raw replay nonce) is a design call for you; and the Appendix A vectors don't exercise the short-ciphertext branch (empty content, 17-byte ciphertext < Nh) or any rejection case, which needs new vectors from an implementation.
